LAKE MIST AT THE SURFACE: a thin white mist lying on the still water, thickest over the deep middle, the far shore fading into it
THICK FOG BANK: a dense grey fog pressing close over the harbour, muffling everything beyond the nearest pilings into soft erasure
THIN MORNING HAZE: a pale gauzy haze sitting just above the water, softening the distant dockside into a watercolour wash
SEA FOG ROLLING IN: cool sea fog advancing steadily across the open water, swallowing the far buoys one by one as it comes
LOW MIST POOLING: wisps of mist collecting in the hollows between hulls, pooling thickest where the water runs coldest and stillest
LIFTING HARBOUR MIST: tattered shreds of mist beginning to rise off the surface, curling upward in slow, lazy spirals from the warmer shallows
COLD CLEAR AIR: sharp, biting cold air sitting over the harbour, every rope and timber edge precise and hard-edged in the stillness
WARM STILL AIR: heavy warm air resting still and heavy over the water, carrying the salt and tar smell of a settled summer afternoon
WASHED CLEAN AFTER RAIN: cool clear air scrubbed fresh by the rain, every plank and piling standing out crisp against the far shore
SALTY CLEAR WITH A BREEZE: a clean salt-edged breeze moving steadily across the harbour, carrying the open-sea smell in from the channel
AUTUMN CRISP AIR: dry, crisp autumn air hanging sharp over the water, faintly scented with kelp and cold stone from the breakwater
CRYSTAL HARBOUR CLARITY: exceptionally clear still air, the far jetty walls and their barnacled bases reading with rare sharpness across the water
LIGHT DRIZZLE VEIL: a fine drizzle hanging in the air as a soft translucent curtain, blurring the far moorings into pale grey shapes
THIN RAIN DRIFTING: thin rain drifting sideways on a gentle harbour wind, prickling the surface and softening every far edge to watercolour
GREY DRIZZLE SETTLING: a steady grey drizzle settling over the whole basin, thickening the air between the boat hulls with fine wet gauze
DRIZZLE AND STILLNESS: a quiet drizzle hanging quietly in the calm air, each drop catching and scattering in the dense humid stillness
STRONG SEA SPRAY: a fine white spray lifting gently off the chop and drifting across the open harbour mouth on a carrying wind
SALT SPRAY AND GUSTS: gusty wind carrying salt spray low over the water as a fine cool haze
WIND-WHIPPED SPRAY: a stiff crosswind lifting a fine spray from the wave crests and carrying it as a soft haze over the harbour
LIGHT SNOW FALLING: small soft snowflakes falling steadily over the water, settling on rope coils and dock planks in a thin white dusting
FLURRY OVER THE HARBOUR: a sudden flurry sweeping across the basin in a pale swirling rush, snowflakes skating sideways on the harbour wind
GENTLE SNOW DRIFTING: large slow snowflakes drifting almost straight down in the calm harbour air, landing on the water with a soft hiss
WOODSMOKE FROM THE CHANDLERY: a thin thread of woodsmoke rolling low from the chandlery chimney, spreading flat and fragrant over the cold water
DOCKSIDE CHIMNEY SMOKE: pale woodsmoke from the dockmaster's stove drifting low across the moorings, carrying the warm smell of burning pine
SMOKE LYING ON THE WATER: woodsmoke from two or three harbourside chimneys pooling down to the surface, lying in lazy slow-moving layers over the basin
